items.title: RL Post-Training in Diffusion Transformers Is Activation Steering
items.summary: RL post‑training boosts diffusion transformers’ visual quality, text rendering, and compositional accuracy by learning complex, input‑dependent transformations.
items.whyItMatters: Tech‑savvy readers care because it enhances AI image generation fidelity and prompt‑specific control, improving practical creative workflows.

items.title: PlayCraft: Designing Engaging Games from Agent Play Experience
items.summary: PlayCraft automates game design by using a vision-based AI agent’s play experience to refine games for mastery and engagement.
items.whyItMatters: It speeds up creating engaging games, saving designers time and improving player retention.

items.title: TideCache: Efficient Hybrid LLM Serving with Transparent Cache Management and Layer-Wise Streaming
items.summary: TideCache is a CPU–GPU hybrid LLM serving system that allocates GPU memory and manages cache residency across GPU and host memory for efficient layer-wise streaming.
items.whyItMatters: It boosts LLM inference speed and resource efficiency, crucial for deploying large models on limited hardware.

items.title: One Prior, Two Dynamics: Repurposing Video Diffusion Transformers for Self-Supervised Latent Action Learning
items.summary: The paper proposes O^2LaF, using a pretrained video diffusion transformer as a prior to learn latent actions and dynamics from visual transitions.
items.whyItMatters: It could accelerate self-supervised learning by leveraging existing generative models for action inference.

items.title: AgentRoboCritic: Understanding the Capability of Frontier Agents on Direct Robot Control
items.summary: The paper analyzes how frontier multimodal agents like GPT-6 Astra execute low-level robot actions, revealing detailed success and failure patterns beyond episode-level metrics.
items.whyItMatters: It helps developers fine-tune robot control and improve safety for AI-driven automation.

items.title: Bio-PM-Guided Synthetic IMU Generation
items.summary: The article discusses using Bio-PM-guided synthetic IMU data to improve human activity recognition models, addressing data scarcity and generalization issues.
items.whyItMatters: Synthetic augmentation can reduce costly data collection and enhance model robustness across diverse users.

items.title: Depth Pro 2: Sharp and Temporally Consistent Metric Monocular Depth
items.summary: Depth Pro 2 delivers dense, metric depth for images and video at full resolution, balancing temporal consistency and boundary sharpness in a single scalable network.
items.whyItMatters: It improves real‑time depth estimation for AR/VR and autonomous systems by providing sharper, temporally stable depth maps.

items.title: SoK: Assessing the Evolution of LLM Capability in Software Vulnerability Research
items.summary: The paper introduces a framework to evaluate how large language model agents discover, validate, and patch software vulnerabilities, highlighting their growing impact on security practices.
items.whyItMatters: It helps security professionals gauge AI tools’ effectiveness and prioritize defenses against automated vulnerability exploitation.

items.title: Active Feature Acquisition by Distilling an Oracle Teacher
items.summary: The paper proposes a method for Active Feature Acquisition that distills knowledge from an oracle teacher to guide feature selection under budget constraints.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a more efficient way to reduce costly data acquisition in machine learning models.

items.title: PGX: Physically Grounded Execution for Long-Horizon Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
items.summary: PGX splits long-horizon humanoid loco‑manipulation into separate temporal and precision modules, using classical training‑free control to improve VLA model performance.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a scalable way to boost complex robot tasks without costly retraining.

items.title: Realized versus Population Reliability: Anytime-Valid Self-Consistency Certification under Correlated Reasoning
items.summary: The paper shows that self-consistency certification for language models fails under correlated reasoning, proposing a new anytime-valid method that controls Type I error.
items.whyItMatters: Tech readers need reliable error bounds for AI outputs, especially when reasoning steps are interdependent.

items.title: Probing the "Conscious" Mind: Selective Access and Global Workspace in Vision-Language Models
items.summary: The paper introduces MC‑Lens, a multimodal Jacobian tool to probe internal concept representations in vision‑language models using Global Workspace Theory.
items.whyItMatters: It offers a new way to understand and improve how VLMs integrate and access visual and textual concepts.

items.title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
items.summary: A passing UVM regression shows the design agrees with the reference model on what the scoreboard checks, not that it meets the specification. Bugs that pass every test yet violate the specification, termed scoreboard escapes, survive mature testbenches. items.title: ProtoDiffusion: Token-per-Layer Generative Modeling of Multi-Layer Images
items.summary: Graphic designs are ordered compositions of RGBA layers whose separation enables selection, movement, and reuse. Existing layered models represent each layer with a full-canvas or region-sized spatial latent grid, so representation size grows with the cumulative spatial extent of the layers. items.title: Represented but misread: Post-training changes how language models read out what they represent
items.summary: Does post-training change what a language model represents, or how this representation is read out into an answer? We compared linear probes with the models' own answers, analyzed with signal detection theory, in six open-weight base models and their post-trained versions. items.title: Text-Aware, Vision-Blind: How Multimodal Image Editing Systems Handle Unsafe Inputs
items.summary: Multimodal image generation systems have made rapid progress and increasingly emphasize content safety. However, their safety mechanisms tend to rely on a single modality and lack joint consideration of both visual content and text prompts, particularly in instruction-guided image editing, where the uploaded image may itself carry risk. items.title: GEOHunter: Mapping a Generative Engine Optimization Network in the Wild
items.summary: Generative engines synthesize retrieved web pages into answers, recommendations, and rankings. Generative engine optimization (GEO) services sell visibility in these answers by publishing promotional articles on user-generated-content (UGC) platforms for paying clients. Such promotion raises concerns in medical and financial domains, where misleading advice can cause harm. To study the severity…

items.title: Multi-institutional grading of Barrett's esophagus dysplasia without stain normalization using a pathology foundation model and multiple instance learning
items.summary: Barrett's esophagus dysplasia grading suffers substantial inter-observer variability, particularly for low-grade dysplasia, complicating clinical decision-making. We conducted a retrospective multi-institutional diagnostic accuracy study of a foundation model-based deep learning system for dysplasia grading, using 969 H\&E-stained whole slide images from four institutions. Patch-level classifiers…

items.title: MM-SystemOneBias: Evaluating Bias in Multimodal Jev-Style System One Decision Models
items.summary: When multimodal decision models determine actions, moderation outcomes, or quality judgments, their reliability depends on preserving semantic decisions across presentation changes, ignoring irrelevant additions, and distinguishing information consistent with task evidence from information that conflicts with it. Existing evaluations study decision-interface biases and multimodal model behavior…

items.title: Replication of Agentic Security Events: Audit and Investigation (ROGUE-AI)
items.summary: Agents based on large language models (LLMs) can now delete files and send payments on behalf of their users. News media reports routinely describe failures of these agents (e.g., Replit's coding agent deleting a production database), but a report often only says what went wrong and rarely (in)validates the incident or finds its root cause.
